name: Nāth initiation (dīkṣā)
method_summary: Entry into the order from a guru in stages: the cutting of the top-knot with the giving of a mantra and the black woollen cord (the aughaṛ stage); after a period of service and probation, the ear-splitting and earrings (darśanī stage), with a new name ending in -nāth and affiliation to a panth.

warnings.text: The would-be disciple is warned of the hardship of the yogī's life before initiation (as depicted in Hīr).

prerequisites: acceptance by a guru; service; the guru's testing

name: Ear-splitting (kān-phaṛāī)
method_summary: At the second initiation the cartilage of both ears is split by a specialist guru and, after healing, the large earrings (darśan/mudrā) are inserted — the defining mark of the Kānphaṭa yogī. Summary only.

warnings.text: A bodily rite performed only by the guru within the order; not a practice to be undertaken by oneself (tradition's rule as reported).

notes: Body-cutting rite: summary only per project rules.

name: Tending the sacred fire (dhūnī)
method_summary: Keeping the yogī's fire burning at the seat or camp, offering to it and distributing its ash (vibhūti) as blessing.

name: Begging with the cry 'alakh'
method_summary: The wandering yogī begs his food calling 'alakh!' (the invisible), receiving alms in his bowl; greetings are exchanged with 'ādeś'.

name: Worship of the guru (guru-pūjā)
method_summary: Daily worship of one's own guru at the three times and offering oneself in mind, deed and speech (KJN 12.7–9); hymns, armour and name-litanies of Gorakṣanātha (Gorakṣaguṭikā).

name: Burial of a yogī in samādhi
method_summary: At death a Nāth yogī is buried seated in a tomb (samādhi) rather than cremated; the tomb becomes a place of worship.

name: Mental worship of the body-liṅga with eight flowers
method_summary: Instead of an external liṅga, the practitioner worships the liṅga within the body mentally, offering the eight inner flowers — non-harming, sense-restraint, compassion, feeling, patience, conquest of anger, meditation and knowledge — and, in the Yogaviṣaya, bathing the inner Lord with the moon's nectar and offering the flower of the mind.

name: Nectar meditations for the conquest of death (mṛtyuñjaya)
method_summary: Contemplating white, cool nectar pouring from the sky through the openings of the body, or oneself seated on a white lotus in the ocean of milk sprinkled from a lotus above, or the full moon at navel, head and heart; said to remove disease, old age and death.

warnings.text: To be given only to a devoted disciple tested (even for a year); kept secret from the deceitful, cruel and undevoted.

signs_of_progress: freedom from disease; youthfulness; forms at will (KJN 5)

name: Arresting grey hair and age (palita-stambhana)
method_summary: A set of meditations on dark nectar in the centres and brahmarandhra, with seclusion and restrained diet, said to restore youth; the text lists eleven successive attainments.
prerequisites: solitary, clean, quiet place; restrained diet (KJN 7.7–9)

name: Meditation on the centres (Kaula)
method_summary: Fixing the mind on a centre — the root, the brahma-knot, the heart, the throat, the palate, the forehead, the brahmarandhra — or on a lamp-flame in the sixty-four-petalled lotus, each with its own signs and powers.

warnings.text: To be given only to a devoted disciple tested (even for a year); kept secret from the deceitful, cruel and undevoted.

signs_of_progress: trembling, shaking, speech in tongues, spontaneous seals, frog-hopping, levitation, knowledge of past and future (KJN 14.16–19)

name: Entering the mind-less state (unmanī-bhāva)
method_summary: Thinking of no element, no above or below, being like wood, making the mind 'void of void', free of thought and motionless, until the jīva is dissolved and not roused by any sound.
signs_of_progress: insensibility to outer sound; freedom from decay (KJN 14.85–86)

name: Making the body adamantine (vajrīkaraṇa)
method_summary: Bhairava's own practice by which he survived dissolution: meditation on the innate centre in the bone-circle and on nested lotuses flooded with milk-white nectar, so that the body stands 'like a thunderbolt'. Summary only.

warnings.text: 'This most secret teaching is to be guarded with effort.'

name: Placing the syllables for liberation (Kaula nyāsa)
method_summary: Placing seed-syllables on the anus, genitals, navel, mouth, nostrils, ears, eyes and forehead; for one in whom it is established, liberation is certain and at death the skull splits.

name: Worship of the circle of yoginīs (Kaula cakra rite)
method_summary: Kaula worship of the sixty-four yoginīs and the eight-by-eight circles in a secluded place with food, fish, meat and wine, with a Śakti partner; recorded only in summary.

warnings.text: To be given only to a devoted disciple tested (even for a year); kept secret from the deceitful, cruel and undevoted.
One fallen from the pledge (samaya) is a paśu; dualistic attitude in the rite is condemned.

name: The non-dual caru rite
method_summary: Kaula consumption, in daily and occasional rites, of substances ordinarily held impure, as a discipline of non-duality; recorded only in summary.

warnings.text: No one may be made to take the caru by force, without their will.
One who, having taken up non-dual conduct, acts otherwise falls into terrible hells.
To be given only to a devoted disciple tested (even for a year); kept secret from the deceitful, cruel and undevoted.

name: Forced departure through the skull (utkrānti)
method_summary: A practice for leaving the body by driving the breath upward so that the skull splits and the jīva goes to the spotless; recorded only as the text's claim, without method.

warnings.text: Presented as a 'proof of liberation' for the adept; the texts keep such teachings secret from the untested.

name: The adept's posture (siddhāsana)
method_summary: One heel pressed at the perineum, the other foot above the genitals, body straight, senses restrained, gaze fixed between the brows; with the lotus one of the two pre-eminent postures, 'opening the door of liberation'.

name: The five seals and locks of the Gorakṣaśataka
method_summary: Mahāmudrā, nabhomudrā (khecarī), uḍḍiyāna, jālandhara and mūlabandha: one who knows them is fit for success; uḍḍiyāna conquers death, jālandhara stops the nectar falling into the fire, mūlabandha draws apāna upward.

warnings.text: The reversed practice is to be obtained from the guru's mouth.

name: The reversed practice (viparīta-karaṇa)
method_summary: Inverting the relation of sun (navel) and moon (palate) — navel above, palate below — so that the nectar is not consumed by the sun.

warnings.text: To be learned from the guru's mouth.

name: Breath-control through moon and sun (Gorakṣaśataka)
method_summary: In the bound lotus, filling through the left (moon) and releasing through the right (sun) while meditating on the moon-disc, then the reverse while meditating on the sun-disc at the navel; this purifies the channels and manifests the inner sound.

warnings.text: Draw in and release the breath slowly; do not hold it beyond measure nor release it hastily.
Avoid pungent, sour and salty food; take milk.

signs_of_progress: sweat, then trembling, then rising up (GŚ 49); purified channels, kindled fire, inner sound, health (GŚ-Briggs 101)
notes: Measures of retention given in the text are not reproduced.

name: The five element-concentrations (Gorakṣaśataka)
method_summary: Holding the mind with the breath on earth (heart, yellow, square, la), water (throat, white crescent, va), fire (palate, red triangle, ra), air (between the brows, smoky circle, ya) and space (brahmarandhra, clear, ha, with Sadāśiva); they stabilise, dissolve, burn, whirl and dry, and the space-concentration opens the door of liberation.
notes: The fixed durations in the text are not reproduced.

name: Meditation with and without qualities (Gorakṣaśataka)
method_summary: With the gaze at the nose-tip, meditating on the centres in their colours (with qualities) and on the attributeless Śiva in the sky and the all-pervading self (without qualities); adjuncts are removed by practice.

name: Seeing the mind with the mind
method_summary: Placing the mind within Śakti and Śakti within the mind, the practitioner beholds the mind by the mind; in the Amaraughaśāsana this, in sahaja-samādhi, is liberation itself.

name: The śāmbhavī seal
method_summary: Attention held on an inner aim while the eyes gaze outward without blinking; the half-open, steady gaze in which breath and mind dissolve.

name: The unrepeated repetition (ajapā japa): 'haṃsa'
method_summary: U21 contribution: in Nāth and Kaula teaching the breath itself repeats 'haṃsa' (heard as 'so 'ham') 21,600 times a day; one is to attend to it constantly ('say haṃsa haṃsa always').

name: Khecarī mudrā
method_summary: U21 contribution: in the Nāth texts the tongue turned back into the cavity above the palate with the gaze between the brows, associated with drinking the nectar and conquering death. Summary only.

warnings.text: Called 'most secret'; to be guarded.
Learned from the guru's mouth.

name: Vajrolī mudrā
method_summary: U21 contribution: a practice for drawing up and preserving bindu, in the context of which the Haṭhapradīpikā says death comes by the fall of bindu and life by its retention. Summary only.

warnings.text: A restricted practice concerning sexual fluids; only its purpose (retention of bindu) is recorded.

name: Stirring of Sarasvatī (sarasvatī-cālana)
method_summary: In the 'original' Gorakṣaśataka a practice for arousing the goddess (kuṇḍalinī) in the central channel; summary only, recalled.

name: Listening to the inner sound
method_summary: U21 contribution: Nāth yogīs attend to the unstruck sound (anahad nād) arising at the heart and resounding in the sky-circle; the nād horn is its outer sign.

name: Cremation-ground practice (Aghora)
method_summary: Dwelling, meditating and performing rites in the cremation ground, smeared with its ash, to overcome fear and disgust and see Śiva in death; recorded only in summary.

warnings.text: Aghora practice is given only by the guru and kept secret; the recent teacher Aghoreśvar Bhagavān Rām is reported to have taught that it is naturalness and service, not spectacle (tradition's account, to be sourced).

name: Practice upon a corpse (śava-sādhana)
method_summary: A rite seated upon a corpse in the cremation ground, attributed to Aghora and Śākta adepts; recorded only as named.

warnings.text: Aghora practice is given only by the guru and kept secret; the recent teacher Aghoreśvar Bhagavān Rām is reported to have taught that it is naturalness and service, not spectacle (tradition's account, to be sourced).

name: Eating and drinking from the skull bowl
method_summary: The Aghora ascetic uses a skull (khappar) as his bowl, as a discipline of non-discrimination; the Kaulajñānanirṇaya calls the skull the best of vessels.

warnings.text: Aghora practice is given only by the guru and kept secret; the recent teacher Aghoreśvar Bhagavān Rām is reported to have taught that it is naturalness and service, not spectacle (tradition's account, to be sourced).

name: Cultivating non-discrimination (abheda)
method_summary: Freeing oneself from the eight fetters — disgust, doubt, fear, shame, loathing, pride of family, of conduct and of caste — by treating nothing as untouchable; the freed one is Maheśvara.

name: Service of the sick and outcaste (Aghora seva)
method_summary: Care of leprosy patients and the destitute as the practice of Aghora, as taught by Aghoreśvar Bhagavān Rām and the Śrī Sarveśvarī Samūh.

name: Pilgrimage to Hiṅglāj
method_summary: Pilgrimage to the Goddess at Hiṅglāj (Balochistan), made by Kīnārām according to tradition and honoured by Aghora and Nāth ascetics.

name: Bathing in the Krīm Kuṇḍ
method_summary: Bathing in the tank at Kīnārām Sthal, Varanasi, held to cure illness and grant blessings, especially on set days.
